spec: Build a REST API for personal notes. Users can create, list, fetch, update and delete notes. Each note has a title, body and timestamps. Notes are stored in DynamoDB.

complexity.rationale: Single DynamoDB-backed entity with ordinary CRUD only.

congruence_checklist: GET endpoint fetching a single note
Note model has title, body and timestamps

plan.summary: A REST API for managing personal notes. Clients (a web/mobile front-end or HTTP client) perform full CRUD operations on notes; each note carries a title, body and created/updated timestamps. The FastAPI service persists notes directly in a DynamoDB table using the AWS SDK (boto3), with no asynchronous or event-driven processing required.

endpoints.purpose: Create a new note from a JSON body containing title and body; generates a UUID id and created_at/updated_at timestamps and stores the item in DynamoDB.
List all notes for the caller, returning the DynamoDB scan/query results with optional limit and pagination cursor.
Fetch a single note by its id; returns 404 if the item does not exist in DynamoDB.
Update the title and/or body of an existing note and refresh its updated_at timestamp.
Delete a note by its id; returns 404 if the item does not exist.
Liveness/readiness probe used by the evaluation harness; confirms the service is up and the DynamoDB table is reachable.

data_models.name: NoteCreateRequest
fields: body: string (optional, defaults to empty string)

data_models.name: NoteListResponse
fields: next_cursor: string | null (opaque pagination token from DynamoDB LastEvaluatedKey)

aws_resources.name: notes
aws_resources.justification: Primary and only datastore required by the spec ('Notes are stored in DynamoDB'). Single table with partition key note_id (string), PAY_PER_REQUEST billing; every CRUD endpoint calls PutItem/GetItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Scan against it.

aws_resources.name: notes_api_service_role
aws_resources.justification: Role plus least-privilege policy granting the notes service GetItem, PutItem, UpdateItem, DeleteItem, Query and Scan on the notes table only; documents the exact permissions the application code requires.

aws_resources.name: /personal-notes-api/application
aws_resources.justification: Log group the FastAPI service writes structured request/error logs to, giving operators visibility into note CRUD failures. This is the only observability sink the application actually calls.

assumptions: 'Personal notes' is interpreted as a single-tenant/personal API: no authentication, user accounts or per-user partitioning are implemented, since the spec mentions none. Notes therefore live in one table keyed only by note_id.
Note ids are server-generated UUID4 strings returned in the create response, rather than client-supplied.
Timestamps are server-generated ISO-8601 UTC strings; created_at is immutable and updated_at is refreshed on every successful update.
PUT is treated as a partial update (only supplied fields change) because the spec says 'update' without specifying replace semantics; unknown fields are rejected.
Listing uses a DynamoDB Scan with a default page size of 50 and an opaque cursor, which is acceptable for personal-scale data volumes.

No asynchronous processing, notifications, file uploads or scheduled jobs are implied, so SQS, SNS, S3, Lambda and API Gateway are deliberately omitted; the service runs as its own process and calls DynamoDB directly.
Table name and AWS endpoint URL (for LocalStack) are supplied to the application via environment variables such as NOTES_TABLE_NAME and AWS_ENDPOINT_URL.
Responses are JSON; errors use standard HTTP status codes (400 validation, 404 missing note, 500 backend failure).

events: 🧭 Parsed specification → personal_notes_api (fastapi); AWS resources: DynamoDB:notes, IAM:notes_api_service_role, CloudWatch:/personal-notes-api/application

🐍 Generated application code (initial): 7 files — FastAPI notes service split into three decoupled modules: `app.py` (routes, dependency-injected repository, exception handlers mapping NoteNotFound->404, InvalidCursor->400, StorageError->500), `models.py` (pydantic v2 models with strict extra=forbid request bodies and partial-update validation), and `storage.py` (a `NotesRepository` interface with a boto3 DynamoDB implementation honouring `AWS_ENDPOINT_URL`/`AWS_DEFAULT_REGION`/`NOTES_TABLE_NAME` plus an in-memory implementation). All CRUD calls use PutItem/GetItem/UpdateItem (conditional, ALL_NEW)/DeleteItem/Scan with base64 opaque pagination cursors derived from LastEvaluatedKey; `/health` describes the table. Tests use `fastapi.testclient.TestClient` with an injected in-memory repo, a fake DynamoDB Table/client, and monkeypatched boto3.resource — entirely offline, no secrets, no debug literals, bind host from env defaulting to 127.0.0.1.

🏗️ Generated Terraform (initial): 4 files — Terraform for personal_notes_api covering exactly the plan's aws_resources: (1) a DynamoDB table `notes` with partition key `note_id` (S), PAY_PER_REQUEST billing, point-in-time recovery and SSE using a customer managed KMS key; (2) a CloudWatch Logs group `/personal-notes-api/application` with 365-day retention and KMS encryption; (3) an IAM role `notes_api_service_role` plus a least-privilege policy granting GetItem/PutItem/UpdateItem/DeleteItem/Query/Scan/DescribeTable on the notes table ARN only, log stream writes scoped to the log group ARN, and KMS use scoped to the single CMK — no wildcard actions or resources. A rotated customer managed KMS key with an explicit key policy backs the encryption requirements for both the table and the log group (Checkov CKV_AWS_119 / CKV_AWS_158 / CKV_AWS_7). Files: versions.tf (terraform block pinning hashicorp/aws ~> 5.0), variables.tf (defaults matching plan resource names), main.tf (provider with project / managed-by default_tags plus all resources), outputs.tf (table name/ARN, log group, role and policy ARNs, KMS ARN for wiring NOTES_TABLE_NAME and friends). Only LocalStack-Community-supported services are used; no S3, SQS, SNS, Lambda or API Gateway were created since the plan explicitly omits them.
